title: feat(search): Unicode-safe fuzzy matching with preview UI

commits.message:
feat(search): add fuzzy subsequence matching with scoring

Implements ROADMAP #17 — fuzzy search for the search plugin.

- Add fuzzy.ts: greedy subsequence matcher with position scoring
  (word-boundary bonus, consecutive-run bonus, gap penalty)
- Export fuzzyMatch / findFuzzyMatches as standalone pure functions
- Integrate fuzzy mode into findSearchMatches / replaceAllMatches
  via a new `fuzzy` option on SearchOptions
- Add 59 tests covering algorithm correctness, edge cases, and
  integration with existing literal/regexp/wholeWord modes

The search plugin previously had no dedicated unit tests for
findSearchMatches / replaceAllMatches; this PR also fills that gap.

feat(search): make fuzzy matching code-point aware

Astral-plane characters (emoji, CJK extension blocks, musical
symbols) span two UTF-16 code units, and the matcher previously
indexed text by code unit — so an emoji in the query could never
match, positions could land inside a surrogate pair, and gaps
containing astral characters were priced double.

- Compare and advance by whole code points in greedyMatch and the
  scan loops; returned offsets stay in UTF-16 code units to match
  editor selection coordinates (CodeMirror, Monaco, textarea)
- Treat emoji as word boundaries by testing the full previous code
  point, so "👋hello" scores "hello" at a boundary
- Measure maxGap and gap penalties in code points, not code units
- Add 12 tests covering emoji/CJK matching, surrogate-pair safety,
  astral case folding, and boundary scoring

feat(electron): add fuzzy search mode with match preview

Surfaces the fuzzy matcher in the demo app so the feature is
verifiable by hand, and keeps typing responsive on large documents.

- Fz toggle (or Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F) switches the search bar to fuzzy
  subsequence matching; replace-all honours the active mode
- Preview row renders the current match window with every matched
  character marked, plus the match score and offsets — subsequence
  matching becomes visible instead of magic
- Search input is debounced (80ms) so re-searching never blocks a
  keystroke; a full fuzzy scan of a 169k-char doc measures ~14ms,
  inside one frame budget
- Add 8 integration tests driving the bar against a real editor
